summary.headline: Maiden Forgings H2 FY26 revenue rose 17.46% YoY to INR122.60 crore, with net profit up 46.37% to INR2.93 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 production of 35,546 metric tons and FY26 revenue of INR233.96 crore, EBITDA of INR17.22 crore and net profit of INR5.02 crore. H2 EBITDA grew only 3.52% YoY to INR10.49 crore, and management attributed the margin improvement in the last three months mainly to a shift toward pneumatic nails, stainless steel bars and alloy steel bars. A new 4-acre integrated facility at Modinagar is being commissioned, with unit shifting already under way, and two new product lines (GI wires and stainless steel machine components) are expected to start around September-October 2026. Management guided to EBITDA margin improvement of at least 1-2% within FY27 but gave few hard numbers, and deferred several questions (realisation, other income, order pipeline, product-mix split) to later email or disclosure.

segments.name: B2B (industrial)
segments.commentary: Management describes B2B as the stable base, serving automotive, engineering, infrastructure and manufacturing customers; the basic products have been sold for about 30 years. No segment-level revenue split was given.

segments.name: B2G / defence
segments.commentary: Registrations obtained with Ordnance Factory Board Kolkata, Ordnance Factory Muradnagar, TBRL DRDO Chandigarh and CEMILAC DRDO Bangalore; supplies made to HAL, BHEL and NTPC. Target of 20-25% of sales from B2G in the mid-term, with no current figure disclosed.

segments.name: B2C / pneumatic nails
segments.commentary: Pneumatic nails are cited as a high-margin product whose sales grew from January 2026; current utilisation of the pneumatic nails facility is about 60-70% (since March/April 2026).

guidance_outlook: FY27: EBITDA margin to rise by at least 1-2 percentage points from current levels, with H1 FY27 improving over the prior year and H2 FY27 a further increase.
Current facility utilisation targeted at about 85% from August-September 2026 after shifting and consolidation; management said 90% is the practical maximum with present machinery.
Current installed capacity of about 53,000 tons; consolidation alone could take output to about 45,000 tons at peak, with FY27 target of about 42,000 tons.
Two new products (GI wires and stainless steel machine components) to add about 9,000-10,000 tons per year, with commercial production around September-October 2026 and a 2-4 month teething period.
Raw material costs expected to rise in FY27, which management expects to be passed through to customers; management expects volumes to be maintained.
capex_capacity: New 4-acre integrated manufacturing facility at Modinagar is consolidating two existing units; unit shifting began April 2026 and management said the new facility is ready to move into and expects it to be operational soon.
Management said the new facility will include a solar installation for part of its energy needs; no capex amount was disclosed.
Capex and growth in FY26 were funded entirely from internal accruals; no equity or institutional borrowing was raised.
Land acquired for expansion over the next five years, per management.
Overseas warehousing: a 100% owned UAE subsidiary was planned for Dubai; groundwork began February 2026 and was postponed due to the geopolitical conflict.
demand_pricing: Management said export order book is the highest in company history, and reoccurring orders are strong despite geopolitical volatility.

Volumes ran at about 3,000 tons per month until September 2025 and about 3,500-3,600 tons per month from November 2025; about 7,000 tons was reported for April-May 2026, with management saying the run rate was maintained.

Management said margin protection relies on back-to-back procurement against customer POs, with inventory held around a plus or minus 5% band; stainless steel carries longer-term, higher-value inventory.
Management said the steel market was falling until November 2025 (compressing margins) and has been two-way since December 2025.
Management is confident that raw material supply is secure via at least 5 vendors with about 10 years of relationships; management also said it expects no volume loss.

qa_highlights.question: What measures protect margins during sharp steel price volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said raw materials are ordered back-to-back against customer POs, so margins are largely hedged; margins were squeezed only during the falling-price phase up to November 2025, and product mix is now lifting margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the medium-term EBITDA margin aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets a 1-2 percentage point improvement in EBITDA margin within FY27 from current levels, and said H2 FY27 would see a further increase.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs product-mix contribution to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 20% of growth would come from the new products' volumes (9,000-10,000 tons), with most new sales coming from product mix; volumes grow 5-10% per year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pneumatic nails utilisation?
Vinit Thakur (Plus91): what are the H1 and H2 margins and sustainable margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 FY27 should improve on last year and H2 would be a good increase on current margins; it framed the maintainable margin as the level reached after the new plant starts.

qa_highlights.question: Economics of GI wire and the new plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said GI wire margins are around 20-25%, roughly double current margins, based on North India supply gaps; no realisation per ton figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income rise sharply (from INR66 lakh to about INR2-2.5 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to explain in this call, saying it would be covered in a separate call, and said it is somewhat related to the B2G segment.

qa_highlights.question: Expected B2G/defence revenue share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 20-25% of sales from B2G in the mid-term, but has no current order pipeline figures and deferred that to email.

risks_watch: H2 FY26 EBITDA growth of 3.52% against 17.46% revenue growth shows thin conversion; FY27 margin recovery depends on mix shift and new plant ramp.
Peak utilisation capped at about 90% with current machinery; further capacity would need new equipment, which management said might come around 2030.
Stainless steel and alloy raw material costs expected to rise due to nickel and other element shortages; the pass-through depends on customer acceptance.
Dubai/UAE warehousing postponed by geopolitical conflict; timing unclear.
Realisation per ton, product-mix split, other income breakup and B2G order pipeline were not disclosed; management promised separate communication.
Management has an intention to move from BSE SME to the main board, with timing undisclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term growth, innovation and defence positioning, but cautious on specifics: several numeric questions (realisation, product-mix split, other income, defence order pipeline) were deferred to email or a later call, and forward targets such as 85-90% utilisation and 1-2% margin uplift were given without detailed backing.
key_quotes: So whatever volatility is going on, whether it's a price rise or a price fall, we are already hedged by that risk because we order our raw materials back-to-back as we get orders from the customer.
Entire growth and capex has been funded through internal accruals.
So, most of the sale has to come from there only during this year as well as in the future.
We will give it in Q3 announcement.
